full_judgment: 5. Mr. Mustafa Niaz Mohammad the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff Opposite Party submitted that the Court below committed no illegality in passing the impugned order and in accepting the valuation given by plaintiff in the plaint. He submitted that the defendant petitioners filed application under Order 7 rule 11 of Code twice. By order dated 23.3.1986 their application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code was rejected. Again order dated 16.4.86 their fresh application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code was again rejected. On their application issue No. 2 regarding valuation was taken up for hearing by taking off of the suit from the peremptory hearing list. The prayer on the part of the defendant petitioner to get the issue No. 2 regarding valuation heard at a belated stage when the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing and the prayer for withdrawing the suit from the list of peremptory hearing was nothing but dilatory tactics to delay the disposal of the suit. He further submitted that the plaintiffs suit being a suit for declaratory decree and consequential relief the same was to be valued under section 7(iv)(c) of the Court Fees Act and the suit is to be valued according to the amount at which the relief sought and valued in the plaint. The plaintiff has rightly valued to suit at Tk. 51,000.00 calculating on the basis of net income derived from the suit land which the plaintiff got by way of inheritance and amicable arrangement with the other co-sharers and not by purchase.
